correctness.rationale: Explicit 28-vertex 42-edge cubic graph; 861 edge-pair constraints. A four-set resolves precisely when its vertex pair-separation masks cover all 861 constraints. Exhausting all 3276 3-subsets rules out smaller edge bases; exhausting all 20475 4-subsets produces exactly 1932 bases and witness \(\{a_0,b_0,c_1,c_4\}\). Pairwise intersection size three yields 17920 exchange edges. Full BFS from each of 1932 roots reaches the whole graph with maximum distance 5. An independent C++17 implementation uses a different numbering, Floyd–Warshall distances, direct injective edge-signature criterion and pairwise basis-intersection exchange construction. Both programs were executed from package source files and produced byte-identical outputs, proving the finite counts by exhaustive integer checks. No infinite extrapolation is made.

originality.rationale: The primary 2016 paper introduces the edge-distance and set-cover formalism, but no flower-snark result. The primary 2021 flower-snark paper explicitly leaves the edge metric dimension open for odd orders at least seven, giving only the nondecisive bounds 3 and 4. The new finite theorem identifies the value at the first unresolved size \(J_7\), counts all 1932 minimum bases, and computes the entire 17920-edge exchange graph including all 1932 eccentricities. Searches of the scientific literature did not reveal a covering numerical or structural classification. Residual priority risk from unindexed tables is acknowledged.
residual_risks: The literature search cannot exclude obscure, unindexed or unpublished enumerations of the exact flower-snark edge-basis graph.

value.rationale: The 2021 flower-snark paper explicitly leaves exact edge metric dimension unsettled for all odd n≥7; J7 is the first unresolved member. This theorem decides its sharp edge landmark number, then classifies all optimal placements quantitatively and gives a complete connected, self-centered one-landmark replacement geometry with exact diameter five. This goes beyond the general bounds and provides a meaningful finite benchmark for the open family and reconfiguration of optimal sensors; no downstream infinite theorem is needed for that value.
